To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of RESI is feasible and practical for the prospective analysis, from an energy security perspective, of power generation sectors in both developed and emerging economies, covering a significant part of energy security aspects.

“the Renewable Energy Security Index (RESI) is a novel, comprehensive, quantitative indicator of the presence of renewable electricity within a national electricity production mix that is useful for energy analysts and policy-makers to assess the energy security of their countries”.
the RESI indicator, based on life cycle assessment and energy systems modelling, can be used for a prospective analysis of the energy security of national electricity generation sectors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a practical energy security indicator, which can be applied to the power generation sector of any country and which can be used to inform energy policy-making processes.
the practical application of the concept of energy security to the analysis of renewable energy technologies in power generation.
a new, practical and robust approach for prospective analysis of energy security.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
renewable energy technologies are found to be a promising and reliable source of power generation from the perspective of energy security.
the presence of renewable technologies within a power sector is a good sign of energy security, but it is not the whole picture.
RESI can be considered as a practical and reliable tool for the prospective analysis and policy-making regarding the energy security of electricity production sectors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

RESI is a practical tool for energy policy-makers to analyse the energy security of their power generation systems, and that RESI values can be used to compare different countries or regions, or even different time periods within a single country.

RESI is a useful tool for energy security assessment of renewable electricity technologies and that it is capable to identify the main energy security challenges that a country may face in the near future.
the use of RESI is found to be a practical and robust tool to assess the energy security of national power generation systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RESI indicator can provide a robust and comprehensive assessment of the energy security performance of power generation sectors.
RESI is a useful indicator to support the decision making process regarding energy security and the role of renewables in the energy mix.
the use of a prospective energy security index can help to guide policy-makers towards the development of a sustainable energy sector.
